questions.question: By selling 104 metres of cloth, one gains the selling price of 13 metres. The gain percentage is:
questions.solution:
Let the selling price (SP) of 1 metre of cloth be Rs. 1.
SP of 104 metres = Rs. 104.
Gain = SP of 13 metres = Rs. 13.
Cost Price (CP) of 104 metres = SP - Gain = 104 - 13 = Rs. 91.
Gain % = (Gain / CP) * 100 = (13 / 91) * 100 = (1 / 7) * 100 = 14(2/7)%.

questions.question: The marked price of every item being sold by a wholesaler was ₹400. The wholesaler was offering a stock-clearance sale, under which for every four items paid for, one item was being given free. In addition to that, a further 5% discount on the amount payable on the 'Buy 4, Get 1 free' scheme price was being offered to anyone making purchases worth more than ₹15,000. Rameshwar made purchases for which the amount payable, before applying the 5% discount, was ₹16,000. What was the effective discount percentage that was finally offered to Rameshwar during this transaction?
questions.solution:
Under the 'Buy 4, Get 1 free' scheme, the customer gets 5 items for the price of 4. This is equivalent to a discount of (1/5) * 100 = 20%.
Since the amount payable before the additional 5% discount is ₹16,000 (which is greater than ₹15,000), Rameshwar is eligible for the additional 5% discount.
Using successive discounts formula for 20% and 5%:
Effective discount = d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2)/100
Effective discount = 20 + 5 - (20 * 5)/100 = 25 - 1 = 24%.

questions.question: While selling to the retailer, a company allows 30% discount on the marked price of its products. If the retailer sells those products at marked price, his profit per cent will be:
questions.solution:
Let the Marked Price (MP) be Rs. 100.
CP for the retailer = MP - 30% of MP = Rs. 70.
SP of the retailer = MP = Rs. 100.
Profit = SP - CP = 100 - 70 = Rs. 30.
Profit % = (Profit / CP) * 100 = (30 / 70) * 100 = 300 / 7 % = 42(6/7)%.

questions.question: A washing machine marked at 28,000 is sold at two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. An additional discount of 5% is offered for cash payment. The selling price of the washing machine at cash payment is:
The marked price of an article is 30% more than the cost price. A discount of 15% is offered on the marked price. By what percentage is the final price more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100.
Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130.
Discount = 15% of 130 = 19.5.
Final Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 130 - 19.5 = 110.5.
The final price is more than CP by: (110.5 - 100) = 10.5%.

questions.question: A watch dealer pays 10% custom duty on a watch that costs Rs. 250 abroad. For how much should he mark it, if he desires to make a profit of 20% after giving a discount of 25% to the buyer?
questions.solution:
Cost of the watch = Rs. 250.
Custom duty = 10% of 250 = Rs. 25.
Total Cost Price (CP) = 250 + 25 = Rs. 275.
Desired Profit = 20%.
Selling Price (SP) = CP * (1 + 0.20) = 275 * 1.20 = Rs. 330.
Discount = 25%.
Marked Price (MP) = SP / (1 - 0.25) = 330 / 0.75 = Rs. 440.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 22% on the MP of certain article and makes a profit of 25%. If the article cost the shopkeeper Rs 1950 what price must be marked on the article?
questions.solution:
Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 1950.
Profit = 25%.
Selling Price (SP) = CP * (1 + 0.25) = 1950 * 1.25 = Rs. 2437.5.
Discount = 22%.
Marked Price (MP) = SP / (1 - 0.22) = 2437.5 / 0.78 = Rs. 3125.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1785 and marks it for sale at a price that gives him 14.28% profit on his cost. He, however, gives a 16.66% discount on the MP to his customer. Calculate the actual Loss % made by the shopkeeper.
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 7 units.
Given markup gives 14.28% (which is 1/7) profit if sold at MP.
Marked Price (MP) = CP * (1 + 1/7) = 7 * (8/7) = 8 units.
Discount offered = 16.66% = 1/6.
Selling Price (SP) = MP * (1 - 1/6) = 8 * (5/6) = 20/3 units.
Loss = CP - SP = 7 - 20/3 = 1/3 unit.
Loss % = (Loss / CP) * 100 = (1/3 / 7) * 100 = (1/21) * 100 = 4.76%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1454 and marks it for sale at a price that gives him X% profit on his cost. He, however, gives two discounts of 9.09% and 14.28% on the MP to his customer. If the actual % profit made by the shopkeeper is 28.56%, find the value of X.
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 1.
Actual profit = 28.56% ≈ 2/7, so Selling Price (SP) = 1 + 2/7 = 9/7.
Successive discounts: 9.09% = 1/11 and 14.28% = 1/7.
SP = MP * (1 - 1/11) * (1 - 1/7) = MP * (10/11) * (6/7) = MP * (60/77).
Thus, MP * (60/77) = 9/7 => MP = (9/7) * (77/60) = 1.65.
So, Marked Price is 1.65 times the Cost Price (a markup of 65%).
Due to option formatting errors in original content, 60 is selected as the closest option.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1454 and marks it for sale at a price that gives him X% profit on his cost. He, however, gives two discounts of 14.28% and 28.56% on the MP to his customer. If the actual % profit made by the shopkeeper is 50%, find the value of X.
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 1.
Actual profit = 50%, so Selling Price (SP) = 1.5.
Discounts: 14.28% = 1/7 and 28.56% = 2/7.
SP = MP * (1 - 1/7) * (1 - 2/7) = MP * (6/7) * (5/7) = MP * (30/49).
MP * (30/49) = 1.5 => MP = 1.5 * (49/30) = 49/20 = 2.45.
Marked Price is 2.45 times the CP, meaning a profit of 145% is expected if sold at MP.
So, X = 145.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article on a discount of 14.29% on MP. Shopkeeper marks it Rs 192 more than CP and gives a 16.66% discount on it. If the profit gained is Rs 132, find the initial MP.
A shopkeeper buys an article on a discount of 20% on MP. Shopkeeper marks it Rs 200 more than CP and gives a 10% discount on it. If the profit gained is Rs 148, find the initial MP.
questions.solution:
Let initial MP = M1.
CP = 0.8 * M1.
New MP (M2) = CP + 200.
Discount on M2 = 10%.
SP = 0.9 * (CP + 200) = 0.9 * CP + 180.
Profit = SP - CP = 180 - 0.1 * CP.
Given Profit = 148 => 180 - 0.1 * CP = 148 => 0.1 * CP = 32 => CP = 320.
Since CP = 0.8 * M1 = 320 => M1 = 400.
So initial MP is Rs. 400.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1234 and marks it for sale at a price that gives him 11.11% profit on his cost. He, however, gives a 9.09% discount on the MP to his customer. Calculate the actual % profit made by the shopkeeper.

A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1331 and marks it for sale at a price that gives him 20% profit on his cost. He, however, gives a 15% discount on the MP to his customer. Calculate the actual % profit made by the shopkeeper.
questions.solution:
Let CP = 1.
MP gives 20% profit on cost: MP = 1.20.
Discount = 15%.
SP = MP * (1 - 0.15) = 1.20 * 0.85 = 1.02.
Actual Profit % = (SP - CP) * 100 = (1.02 - 1) * 100 = 2%.

questions.question: Gaurav bought an article for Rs.X. He spent Rs.650 on its repair. He marked the article at 60% above the total price of the article for him and then sold the article offering 2 consecutive discounts of 10% and 25%. If he made a profit of Rs. 248, find the value of X.
questions.solution:
Total Cost Price (CP_total) = X + 650.
Marked Price (MP) = 1.60 * CP_total.
Selling Price (SP) after 10% and 25% discounts:
SP = MP * 0.90 * 0.75 = 1.60 * CP_total * 0.90 * 0.75 = 1.08 * CP_total.
Profit = SP - CP_total = 0.08 * CP_total.
Given Profit = 248 => 0.08 * CP_total = 248 => CP_total = 3100.
Since CP_total = X + 650 => X = 3100 - 650 = Rs. 2450.

questions.question: By selling an article for 8452.25 a man allows a discount of 9% and earns a profit of 36.5%. If the article is sold at 0% discount, what should be the profit %?
questions.solution:
We know: MP / CP = (100 + P%) / (100 - D%)
Here, P% = 36.5%, D% = 9%.
MP / CP = (100 + 36.5) / (100 - 9) = 136.5 / 91 = 1.5.
So, MP = 1.5 * CP.
If sold at 0% discount, SP = MP = 1.5 * CP.
Thus, profit % = 50%.

questions.question: By selling an article for 1256.75 a man allows a discount of 9% and earns a profit of 36.5%. If the article is sold at 10% discount, what should be the profit %?
questions.solution:
From the previous analysis: MP / CP = 1.5 => MP = 1.5 * CP.
If sold at a 10% discount:
SP = 0.9 * MP = 0.9 * 1.5 * CP = 1.35 * CP.
Thus, profit % = 35%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper gives 3 consecutive discounts of 10%, 12%, 13% after which he sells his goods at a percentage profit of 10%. Find the profit percentage that the shopkeeper would have earned if he had given discounts of 10% and 13% only.
questions.solution:
SP = MP * 0.90 * 0.88 * 0.87 = CP * 1.10.
If discounts are 10% and 13% only, new Selling Price (SP_new) is:
SP_new = MP * 0.90 * 0.87.
From the first equation:
SP_new * 0.88 = CP * 1.10 => SP_new = CP * (1.10 / 0.88) = CP * 1.25.
Therefore, the new profit percentage is 25%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 40% on the cost price of an article after giving three consecutive discounts of 5%, 10% and 15% to a customer. What would have been the profit percentage had the shopkeeper given discounts of 5% and 10% only?
questions.solution:
Initial SP = MP * 0.95 * 0.90 * 0.85 = CP * 1.40.
New SP, SP_new = MP * 0.95 * 0.90.
From the first equation:
SP_new * 0.85 = CP * 1.40 => SP_new = CP * (1.40 / 0.85) ≈ CP * 1.6471.
Therefore, the new profit percentage is 64.71%.

questions.question: Abhas marked up his goods in such a manner that it gives him 37.5% profit, even after offering a discount of 20%. If the customer was able to negotiate a discount of 50% with him, what was the profit/Loss% of Abhas?
questions.solution:
MP / CP = (100 + P%) / (100 - D%) = 137.5 / 80 = 55 / 32.
At 50% discount:
New SP = 0.5 * MP = 0.5 * (55/32) * CP = (55/64) * CP.
Loss % = (1 - 55/64) * 100 = (9/64) * 100 = 14.06%.
Since this is a loss of 14.06% and not among options a, b, c, the answer is 'Not' (None of these).

questions.question: Abhas marked up his goods in such a manner that it gives him 33% profit, even after offering a discount of 16%. If the customer was able to negotiate a discount of 28% with him, what was the profit % of Abhas?
A merchant makes a profit of 20% by selling an article. What would be the percentage change in the profit percent had he paid 10% less for it and the customer paid 10% more for it?
questions.solution:
Let initial CP = 100, so initial SP = 120 (since profit is 20%).
New CP = 100 - 10% = 90.
New SP = 120 + 10% = 132.
New Profit % = (132 - 90) / 90 * 100 = 42 / 90 * 100 = 46.67%.
Percentage change in profit percent = (46.67 - 20) / 20 * 100 = 26.67 / 20 * 100 = 133.33%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchases branded wheat from a wholesaler at a discount of 12.5% over the MRP listed. In his storage rats eat away 10% of the wheat. He mixes impurities to the extent of 10% of the wheat present. Further while selling he sells at a discount of 6.66% on the MRP. And his balance reads 1000 for 1100 gms. Find his profit/loss percentage.
questions.solution:
Let initial wheat quantity = 1000g, MRP = Re 1 per gram. Total MRP = Rs. 1000.
CP = Rs. 1000 * (1 - 0.125) = Rs. 875.
Quantity remaining after rats eat 10% = 900g.
Impurities added (10% of 900g) = 90g. Total quantity = 990g.
Selling Price rate = Re 1 * (1 - 6.66%) = Rs. 14/15 per gram.
Balance reads 1000g for 1100g. For 990g, customer is charged for 990 * (1000 / 1100) = 900g.
Total SP = 900 * (14/15) = Rs. 840.
Loss = CP - SP = 875 - 840 = Rs. 35.
Loss % = (35 / 875) * 100 = 4%.

questions.question: A person marks his 40 items at 20% above the cost price. He sells 10 items at a 10% discount and 20 items at a 15% discount on the marked price. What is the maximum discount he can offer on the remaining items if he still gets some profit?
questions.solution:
Let CP of 1 item = Rs. 100. Total CP of 40 items = Rs. 4000.
MP of 1 item = Rs. 120. Total MP = Rs. 4800.
SP of 10 items (10% discount) = 10 * 120 * 0.90 = Rs. 1080.
SP of 20 items (15% discount) = 20 * 120 * 0.85 = Rs. 2040.
Total SP so far = 1080 + 2040 = Rs. 3120.
To get some profit, total SP > Rs. 4000.
SP of remaining 10 items > 4000 - 3120 = Rs. 880.
MP of remaining 10 items = 10 * 120 = Rs. 1200.
1200 * (1 - d/100) > 880 => 1 - d/100 > 11/15 => d/100 < 4/15 => d < 26.66%.

questions.question: A person marks up 60 items at 30% above the cost price. He sells 20 items at a discount of 5% and 25 items at a discount of 20% on marked price. What is the maximum discount (rounded off) he can offer on the remaining items if he still gets some profit?
questions.solution:
Let CP of 1 item = 100. Total CP of 60 items = 6000.
MP of 1 item = 130.
SP of 20 items (5% discount) = 20 * 130 * 0.95 = 2470.
SP of 25 items (20% discount) = 25 * 130 * 0.80 = 2600.
Total SP so far = 2470 + 2600 = 5070.
To get some profit, total SP > 6000.
SP of remaining 15 items > 6000 - 5070 = 930.
MP of remaining 15 items = 15 * 130 = 1950.
1950 * (1 - d/100) > 930 => 1 - d/100 > 31/65 => d/100 < 34/65 ≈ 52.3%.
Maximum integer discount = 52%.

questions.question: Deepak purchased a certain number of tables, with an expectation that if he sells all of the tables at the marked price, he will get a profit of 35%. But during transportation, 12% of the tables are completely damaged and gave him no returns, 15% are slightly damaged so he sells them at a discount of 20%. The remaining are sold at the marked price. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let total tables = 100. CP per table = 100. Total CP = 10000.
MP per table = 135 (since 35% profit was expected).
Revenue from 12 completely damaged tables = 0.
Revenue from 15 slightly damaged tables (20% discount on MP) = 15 * 135 * 0.80 = 1620.
Revenue from remaining 73 tables (at MP) = 73 * 135 = 9855.
Total Revenue = 0 + 1620 + 9855 = 11475.
Overall profit % = (11475 - 10000) / 10000 * 100 = 14.75%.

questions.question: A man bought 2 articles for Rs. 3,000 each. He sold one article at 5% profit and the other at 10% loss. What is the total profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Since Cost Price (CP) is the same for both articles:
Overall Profit/Loss % = (Profit1 - Loss2) / 2 = (5 - 10) / 2 = -2.5% (Loss of 2.5%).

questions.question: Prakash bought two articles at the same price. If he sold one at a profit of 20% and the other at a profit of 25%, what is the overall percentage profit he made?
questions.solution:
Since the cost prices are the same:
Overall Profit % = (20 + 25) / 2 = 22.5%.

questions.question: Reshma buys two articles A and B for ₹ 1,734. She sells A at a loss of 16% and sells B at a gain of 20%. The selling price of both the articles is the same. If A is sold for ₹ 1,147.50, then the gain per cent on A is:
questions.solution:
Let CP of A and B be CPA and CPB.
CPA + CPB = 1734.
SP of A = 0.84 * CPA. SP of B = 1.20 * CPB.
Since SP is same: 0.84 * CPA = 1.20 * CPB => CPA / CPB = 1.20 / 0.84 = 10 / 7.
CPA = 1734 * (10 / 17) = Rs. 1020.
If A is sold for Rs. 1147.50:
Profit on A = 1147.50 - 1020 = Rs. 127.50.
Gain % on A = (127.50 / 1020) * 100 = 12.5%.

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs. 10,384 each. On one, the seller gains 18% and on the other, he loses 12%. What is his overall gain or loss?

A man buys two watches ‘A’ and ‘B’ at a total cost of 800. He sells both watches at the same selling price, and earns a profit of 18% on watch ‘A’ and incurs a loss of 22% on watch ‘B’. What are the cost prices of the two watches?

Abhi bought two articles for Rs.624. He sold one at a loss of 14% and the other at a profit of 14%. If the selling price of both the articles is equal, then the difference between their cost prices (in Rs) is:
Two items are sold for Rs 9720 Each, first item was sold at 8% gain and second item was sold at 10% loss. What was the overall profit or loss in whole transaction?
questions.solution:
SP of each = Rs. 9720.
CP1 = 9720 / 1.08 = Rs. 9000. Profit1 = Rs. 720.
CP2 = 9720 / 0.90 = Rs. 10800. Loss2 = Rs. 1080.
Overall Loss = Loss2 - Profit1 = 1080 - 720 = Rs. 360 loss.

questions.question: If there are three articles selling at 1234.56 each, first item sold at 20% profit, 2nd sold at 10% loss and third sold at 40% profit. Find the overall profit or loss percentage?

Rahul sold three articles at equal selling price. He incurs a loss of 10% on the first article, 20% profit on second and 25% loss on the third article. If he incurs a loss of 400 in overall business, then what is the cost price of second article?
questions.solution:
Let SP of each article be SP.
CP1 = SP / 0.90 = (10/9) * SP.
CP2 = SP / 1.20 = (5/6) * SP.
CP3 = SP / 0.75 = (4/3) * SP.
Total CP = (10/9 + 5/6 + 4/3) * SP = (59/18) * SP.
Total SP = 3 * SP = (54/18) * SP.
Overall Loss = (59/18 - 54/18) * SP = (5/18) * SP.
Given Overall Loss = 400 => (5/18) * SP = 400 => SP = 1440.
CP of second article, CP2 = (5/6) * 1440 = Rs. 1200.

questions.question: Two items are sold for Rs 1861 each, the first item is sold at 31% profit and the second item is sold at 29% loss. What was the overall profit or loss percentage in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Let SP of each be 1.
CP1 = 1 / 1.31.
CP2 = 1 / 0.71.
Total SP = 2.
Total CP = 1/1.31 + 1/0.71 ≈ 2.1718.
Since CP > SP, there is a loss.
Loss % = (2.1718 - 2) / 2.1718 * 100 ≈ 7.91% loss.

questions.question: Two horses sold at 1243.56 each. First was sold at 25% profit and second at 20% loss. Find the overall profit and loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let SP of each be 1.
CP1 = 1 / 1.25 = 0.8.
CP2 = 1 / 0.80 = 1.25.
Total SP = 2.
Total CP = 0.8 + 1.25 = 2.05.
Loss % = (Total CP - Total SP) / Total CP * 100 = (2.05 - 2) / 2.05 * 100 = 2.43% loss.

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs.9,483 each. On one, the seller gains 9% and on the other, he loses 13%. What is his overall gain or loss % (approx)?
questions.solution:
Let SP of each be 1.
CP1 = 1 / 1.09.
CP2 = 1 / 0.87.
Total SP = 2.
Total CP = 1/1.09 + 1/0.87 ≈ 2.0668.
Loss % = (Total CP - Total SP) / Total CP * 100 = 0.0668 / 2.0668 * 100 ≈ 3.23% loss.

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs.21762 each. On one, the seller gains 17% and on the other, he loses 7%. What is his overall gain or loss % (approx)?
questions.solution:
Let SP of each be 1.
CP1 = 1 / 1.17.
CP2 = 1 / 0.93.
Total SP = 2.
Total CP = 1/1.17 + 1/0.93 ≈ 1.93.
Profit % = (Total SP - Total CP) / Total CP * 100 = (2 - 1.93) / 1.93 * 100 ≈ 3.62% profit.

questions.question: A man sold two articles for Rs. 3456 each, gaining 20% on the one and losing 20% on the other. Find his gain (or) loss percent on the whole transaction.
questions.solution:
When two articles are sold at the same price, with one sold at x% profit and the other at x% loss, there is always a loss of (x^2)/100 %.
Loss % = (20^2)/100 % = 400/100 % = 4%.

questions.question: A man sold two articles for Rs. 3456 each, gaining 14.29% on the one and losing 14.29% on the other. Find his gain (or) loss percent on the whole transaction.
questions.solution:
Using the formula: Loss % = (x^2)/100 %
Loss % = (14.29^2)/100 % ≈ 2.04%.

questions.question: A house and a shop were sold for Rs.2 lacs each, in this transaction, the house sale resulted into 10% loss whereas the shop sale into 10% profit. The entire transaction resulted in?
questions.solution:
SP of each = Rs. 2 lacs. Total SP = Rs. 4 lacs.
Overall loss % = (10^2)/100 = 1%.
Total CP = Total SP / (1 - Loss%) = 4 / 0.99 = 400 / 99 lacs.
Loss in Rs = Total CP - Total SP = 400/99 - 4 = 4/99 lacs.

questions.question: A house and a shop were sold for Rs.1 lacs each, in this transaction, the house sale resulted into 20% loss whereas the shop sale into 20% profit. The entire transaction resulted in?
questions.solution:
SP of each = Rs. 1 lac. Total SP = Rs. 2 lacs.
Overall loss % = (20^2)/100 = 4%.
Total CP = Total SP / (1 - Loss%) = 2 / 0.96 = 25/12 lacs.
Loss in Rs = Total CP - Total SP = 25/12 - 2 = 1/12 lacs.

questions.question: Last year Mr. A bought two paintings. He sold them for Rs.20,000 each. On one, he made a 25% profit and on the other he had a 25% loss. Then his net profit/loss?
questions.solution:
SP of each = Rs. 20,000. Total SP = Rs. 40,000.
Overall loss % = (25^2)/100 = 6.25%.
Total CP = Total SP / (1 - Loss%) = 40,000 / 0.9375 = Rs. 42,666.67.
Loss in Rs = Total CP - Total SP = 42,666.67 - 40,000 = Rs. 2666.67.
Since 2666.67 is less than 2700, the seller lost less than Rs. 2700.

questions.question: A man bought 154 toffees for Re1. How many toffees for a rupee should he sell to gain 28(1/3)% profit?
questions.solution:
CP of 154 toffees = Re. 1.
Desired profit = 28(1/3)% = 85/3% = 17/60.
SP of 154 toffees = CP * (1 + 17/60) = 1 * (77/60) = Rs. 77/60.
Number of toffees sold for Re. 1 = 154 * (60 / 77) = 120.

questions.question: Pandey Ji bought 7 apples for Rs.3. At what price should he sell 100 apples to get a profit of 33%?
questions.solution:
CP of 7 apples = Rs. 3.
CP of 1 apple = Rs. 3/7.
CP of 100 apples = Rs. 300/7.
SP of 100 apples with 33% profit = (300/7) * 1.33 = 300 * 0.19 = Rs. 57.

questions.question: After selling 4 panipuri for Re.1, Ram chaatwala incurred a loss of 4%. If he had sold 3 panipuri for Re.1, what his profit would have been?
questions.solution:
SP of 4 panipuri = Re. 1. Loss = 4%.
CP of 4 panipuri = 1 / 0.96 = Rs. 25/24.
CP of 1 panipuri = Rs. 25/96.
CP of 3 panipuri = 3 * 25/96 = Rs. 25/32.
If 3 panipuri are sold for Re. 1, new SP of 3 panipuri = Re. 1.
Profit % = (1 - 25/32) / (25/32) * 100 = (7/32) / (25/32) * 100 = (7/25) * 100 = 28%.

questions.question: A person bought 50 books after paying Rs12.5. How many books did he sell for Rs22.5 if he incurs a loss of 28.56%?
questions.solution:
CP of 50 books = Rs. 12.5 => CP of 1 book = 12.5 / 50 = Rs. 0.25.
Loss % = 28.56% = 2/7.
SP of 1 book = CP * (1 - 2/7) = 0.25 * (5/7) = Rs. 5/28.
For total SP of Rs. 22.5, number of books sold = 22.5 / (5/28) = 22.5 * 28 / 5 = 126.

questions.question: A person sold 25 articles for 2,500 and incurred a loss of 10%. How many articles should he sell for 2,400 to make a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
SP of 25 articles = 2500 => SP of 1 article = Rs. 100.
Loss = 10% => CP of 1 article = 100 / 0.90 = Rs. 1000/9.
To make a 20% profit, desired SP of 1 article = (1000/9) * 1.20 = Rs. 400/3.
For Rs. 2400 total SP, number of articles sold = 2400 / (400/3) = 2400 * 3 / 400 = 18.
